subject: Discovery recap & next steps — inference cost reduction for Veridian Bank
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@veridianbank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap & next steps — inference cost reduction for Veridian Bank

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Pain points: 
- Per-inference costs are a primary blocker for broader rollout of your NLP features (customer support triage + fraud detection).
- Current ~2–3x token cost vs target for budgeted monthly API spend.
- Spiky QPS during business hours (daily peaks ~500–800 qps) causing either latency spikes or large provisioned overhead.

Current stack: 
- In-house service that calls a mix of hosted model endpoints (public cloud) and a small on-prem model for sensitive flows.
- No consistent KV/prefix caching today; some limited batching in the frontend.

Success criteria (what would make this a win for Veridian):
- 25–35% unit cost reduction for production inference without increasing p95 latency beyond ~150ms for critical routes.
- Maintain or improve model quality (no meaningful regression on the triage classifier).
- Clear rollout path for sensitive data flows (VPC or private deployment + KMS).

What we propose / what we can help with: 
- Evaluate batching + prefix/KV cache to cut token compute; initial modeling shows common prefixes across customer messages we can cache.
- Quantization options (8-bit / 4-bit) if your accuracy tests are tolerant — we can run quick evals on your sample prompt set.
- Dedicated capacity or private deployment for data residency and consistent latency.

Next steps (agreed):
1) I’ll send an initial pricing sketch and an architecture note that maps batching/caching approaches to your traffic shape. (Attached: redwood_pricing_preview.xlsx)
2) You’ll share a small eval prompt set and a 24–48h sample of inference request metadata (anonymized) so we can simulate batching and estimate savings.
3) Tide over procurement questions: please let us know if SOC2 artifacts / contract templates are needed — we can loop Legal+Security.

If that matches your notes, I’ll follow up with the attachments and a proposed 30-minute technical working session next week to scope the POC.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachment: redwood_pricing_preview.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@veridianbank.com>

Cc: Procurements <procurements@veridianbank.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 09:02:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps — inference cost reduction for Veridian Bank

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap — that aligns with what I captured. A few clarifications from our side: 
- The 25–35% cost reduction would be ideal; we’re prepared to accept up to a 10% latency increase if cost savings are strong, but p95 >200ms would be a hard no for the triage route.
- For sensitive flows, we need either VPC-enabled private deployment or an on-prem option; can you confirm both are available and what the rough SLA/lead time looks like?
- Procurement will want SOC2 evidence and a preliminary SOW estimate. I’ve looped our procurements mailbox.

I’ll share an anonymized 48-hour sample of request logs by EOD tomorrow — let me know preferred format (CSV or newline JSON).

Samir Patel
Head of AI Platforms, Veridian Bank
